# N08. PROJCOL: the attention output projection keeps the NVFP4 column-wise copy of its input from the forward

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

[Index](../KERNELS.md) · Switch: `AK_PROJCOL=1` (config L30) · In the submitted runs: **on** · Class: **E0** · Rule basis: Graph Execution (TR-8.3)

**L4 v3.** This item is L4 v2's, byte for byte, in L4 v3's image (module `17f0403a`). Where this write-up names L4 v2's results, image or test runs, that evidence was collected on L4 v2's package (`firmus_gb300_ngpu8_llama8b_l4_nvfp4_v2`, withdrawn from this submission; see [Index](../KERNELS.md)). This package's own ten runs print the same check line, all `True` (Evidence).

## In brief

In NVIDIA's recipe, Megatron-Core tells Transformer Engine's (TE's) attention output projection (`linear_proj`) to save
its bf16 input for the backward instead of a quantized copy. TE therefore quantizes that input to NVFP4 twice: row-wise
in the forward, and again column-wise, with the random Hadamard transform, in the backward. N8 clears that flag when
each attention layer is built, so TE runs its default mode: one forward call quantizes both usages and the column-wise
copy is kept for the backward. The input quantizer rounds to nearest and reads the same input both times, so the kept
copy has the bytes the backward would have computed. The cost is memory: about 34 MB of NVFP4 data per layer.
**Result:** PASS: byte-identical to stock in the kit and the first-call checks on this image (smoke run and all ten
scored runs), and in the tests of the module's own action on L4 v2's image (same module).

## What it replaces (Replaces)

Terms: **NVFP4** is TE's 4-bit format (E2M1 values, one E4M3 scale per block of 16 values, an fp32 per-tensor scale
from the amax, the largest absolute value). A TE NVFP4 tensor can hold a **row-wise** copy, which feeds the forward
GEMM, and a **column-wise** copy, the transposed layout the weight-gradient GEMM reads. **RHT** is TE's 16×16 random
Hadamard transform, applied to the column-wise copy of activations and gradients before quantization; TE takes the
column-wise amax after it (a "Hadamard amax" pass).

The stock code (Megatron-Core `f6c33bde`, the commit this package builds; TE lines read on TE `131157b5`, the TE of dev
image 0929, NVIDIA's 2026-09-29 release image on which the kernels were developed; this package builds TE 2.20.0 at
`5b28d7aa`, 7 commits later):

- **Megatron sets the flag.** At the end of `Attention.__init__` (`megatron/core/transformer/attention.py` L432-448),
  when `linear_proj` is TE's `Linear` and the run is FP4 (TE ≥ 2.7.0.dev0) or FP8 with a recipe other than delayed
  scaling, Megatron calls `set_save_original_input(self.linear_proj)`, which sets the module's `save_original_input` to
  True (`megatron/core/extensions/transformer_engine.py`, stock L3819-3831). Megatron's comment (L444-447): the core
  attention's output is saved by itself, so also saving its quantized copy in `linear_proj` would cost memory.
- **TE with the flag set** (`transformer_engine/pytorch/module/linear.py`): the forward asks the input quantizer for the
  column-wise usage only when `save_original_input` is False, so it quantizes the input row-wise only (L518-532) and
  saves the bf16 input itself (L692-694). The backward quantizes the saved input again, column-wise only (L1300-1311):
  for the recipe's NVFP4 input quantizer, a second Hadamard amax pass and RHT cast of the same `[8192, 2, 4096]` input
  in every layer.
- **With N8** the flag is cleared right after `Attention.__init__`, so `linear_proj` runs in TE's default mode
  (`save_original_input=False`; `linear.py` L1994, L2027): the forward quantizes the input row-wise and column-wise in
  one call (L524-532); after the forward GEMM TE drops the row-wise data and saves the column-wise copy (L696-717); the
  backward finds the input already quantized and uses that copy (L1294-1296).
- **Not replaced:** any kernel. N8 adds none; each quantize runs the code it would run without N8. In the submitted configuration that is TE's quantize or N6's wrapper of it (Enablement).
- **Where it applies:** every `linear_proj` on which Megatron set the flag, one per transformer layer (32 in the
  submitted runs: "cleared on 32 module(s)", `result_1.txt` L875).

## Why the result is the same (Equivalence)

**Class E0: the output, the input gradient and the weight gradient of `linear_proj` are byte-identical to the stock
path on every tested input.**

Notation: `x` is `linear_proj`'s bf16 input (the core attention's output), `W` its weight, `dy` the incoming gradient.
`Q(x; usage)` is the input quantizer applied to `x` with the given usages.

```text
NVIDIA (save_original_input = True):
  forward   q_r = Q(x; row)                          y  = GEMM(q_r, W)            saved: x (bf16)
  backward  q_c = Q(x; column, RHT)                  dW = wgrad GEMM(dy, q_c)     dx = dgrad GEMM(dy, W)

N8 (save_original_input = False, TE's default):
  forward   (q_r', q_c') = Q(x; row + column, RHT)   y  = GEMM(q_r', W)           saved: q_c'
  backward                                           dW = wgrad GEMM(dy, q_c')    dx = dgrad GEMM(dy, W)

Claim: q_r' = q_r and q_c' = q_c, byte for byte (data, scales and amax of each copy).
```

- **Same input.** Both paths quantize the same `x`. The stock backward re-reads the saved `x`, which nothing changes
  between the forward and the backward (Assumptions).
- **Same quantizer, no randomness.** The input quantizer rounds to nearest: no stochastic rounding, no random number
  generator. Its output is a function of the input and the quantizer's settings alone, so a combined call and two
  single-usage calls with the same settings give the same bytes for each usage.
- **TE's own rule says the same.** TE honours `save_original_input` only for an input quantizer that is safe to
  re-quantize, else ignores it with a warning (`linear.py` L404-430, `module/_common.py` L58-67); for NVFP4: "NVFP4
  quantization is replay-safe unless stochastic rounding is enabled" (`tensor/nvfp4_tensor.py` L257-259).
- **Everything downstream follows.** The forward GEMM gets the same row-wise operand, so `y` is equal. The
  weight-gradient GEMM gets the same column-wise operand and the same `dy`, so `dW` is equal. The input gradient `dx`
  does not read `x` at all.
- **Measured:** at run time, the first eager call compares the combined quantize with a row-only and a column-only
  quantize of the same input, every buffer as bytes (Enablement); the tests compare whole outputs and gradients
  (Evidence).

**State kept between calls:** none that a later call reads for its result. The module keeps a count of cleared
modules, a one-time "checked" flag and a nesting counter that tells the quantize hook it is inside a cleared
`linear_proj` forward (read from `ak_l8b_projcol.py` L23, L76-81, L108). TE keeps the column-wise copy from a layer's
forward to its backward in the same iteration, as it keeps any saved tensor: +34 MB of NVFP4 data per layer (8,192 × 2
× 4,096 values at 4 bits = 33,554,432 bytes), plus its scales; 1,073,741,824 bytes (1 GiB) of data over the 32 layers.

## Numerics (Numerics)

NVFP4, as stock: the same input quantizer, with the same settings, on the same input (E2M1 values, one E4M3 scale per
16 values, an fp32 per-tensor scale from the amax, the RHT on the column-wise copy, round to nearest). Only the time at
which the column-wise copy is made changes: in the forward instead of the backward. The GEMMs and their bf16 outputs
are TE's, with identical operands.

## Optimizer and gradient clipping (Optimizer, Gradient clipping)

Not applicable: N8 changes no optimizer step, and neither computes nor applies the clip coefficient; the weight
gradient it feeds is byte-identical.

## Inputs it accepts (Shape specialisation)

### Gate

- **Where N8 acts.** After the stock `Attention.__init__` returns, if the instance has a `linear_proj` whose
  `save_original_input` is True, N8 sets it to False, counts it and wraps that module's forward (module L89-95).
  Otherwise it does nothing. So N8 acts exactly where Megatron set the flag. There is no shape, dtype or layer test.
- **The forward wrapper** only marks that a call is inside a cleared `linear_proj` forward, and only until the first
  check has run; after that it passes every call straight through (L71-83).
- **The check's trigger:** the first `NVFP4Quantizer.quantize_impl` call with both usages inside a cleared `linear_proj`
  forward, outside CUDA-graph capture (L103-109); once per process.
- **The recipe's call:** the input `[8192, 2, 4096]` bf16, row and column usage, RHT on, stochastic rounding off
  (`result_1.txt` L875). For an input quantizer that is not safe to re-quantize (for NVFP4, one with stochastic
  rounding) TE ignores the flag and quantizes both usages in the forward anyway (`linear.py` L404-430).

### Assumptions not checked in code

1. **Nothing writes `linear_proj`'s input between its forward and its backward.** The stock backward re-quantizes the
   saved input; N8's backward uses the copy made in the forward.
   - Kept true by: the input is the core attention's output, which attention also keeps for its own backward
     (Megatron's comment, `attention.py` L444-447). Nothing in the recipe writes it in place.
   - If it failed: the stock path would quantize the changed input and N8 the original one, so the weight gradients
     would differ. A write that autograd tracks makes the stock backward raise, because TE saves the input with
     `ctx.save_for_backward` (`linear.py` L692-694, L714-717, L1853-1854). Under N8 `linear_proj` no longer saves the
     bf16 input, so such a write raises only if another saved use of the tensor catches it. A write that autograd does
     not track: SILENT.
2. **The input quantizer rounds to nearest.** N8 does not check it.
   - Kept true by: NVIDIA's NVFP4 recipe uses stochastic rounding for gradients only (the index, "Numeric formats");
     the check line shows `SR False` (`result_1.txt` L875).
   - If it failed: no wrong result. TE ignores `save_original_input` for such a quantizer (`linear.py` L404-430), so the
     stock path would be N8's path. N8's first-call check does not replay the random number generator (module L39-69).
3. **The input quantizer is TE's `NVFP4Quantizer`.** The check hooks only that class.
   - Kept true by: the recipe trains with NVFP4 linear layers.
   - If it failed (for example an FP8 recipe, for which Megatron also sets the flag): N8 would still clear the flag, but
     its check would never run, and the run-start gate's `projcol` row, which needs the check done, would raise before
     `run_start` (`firmus_ak/run_start_gate.py` L43-46). RAISE.
4. **The first quantize with both usages in a cleared forward is the input's.** The check takes that call, whatever it
   quantizes.
   - Kept true by: TE quantizes the input before the weight (`linear.py` L500-536, then the weight from L545). The line
     names `[8192, 2, 4096] torch.bfloat16`, the input (`result_1.txt` L875).
   - If it failed: the check would compare a weight's quantize instead, and the input's combined quantize would run
     without N8's check. SILENT, though not a wrong result by itself.
5. **No caller catches the check's exception.** The check marks itself done before comparing (module L108-109).
   - Kept true by: nothing in the recipe catches these exceptions; a failure ends the job before `run_start`.
   - If it failed: a caller that caught the exception would run unchecked afterwards, and the run-start gate would count
     the part as checked. Without such a caller: RAISE.

### Benchmark detection

The flag test reads Megatron's own flag on its own module; the check tests the quantizer's usages and whether a CUDA
graph is being captured. There is no shape constant and no test of the model, the layer count or the process name. The
development version also required the program name to contain "pretrain"; the shipped module does not test it
(Benchmark detection is not allowed, TR-2.3).

## How it is switched on and checked at run time (Enablement)

- **Switch:** `AK_PROJCOL=1` (config L30). Read once at import (module L22),
  default `"0"`; only the value `1` arms it, and otherwise the module installs nothing. No kernel directory.
- **Arming:** the `Attention.__init__` wrapper clears the flag on each `linear_proj` as Megatron builds it (module
  L89-95). If either hooked module is already imported when `ak_l8b_projcol` loads, it is patched at once (L137-140).
- **First-call check** (module L39-69, called at L103-109): in the submitted runs, in the forward of NVIDIA's warm-up
  iteration 0, before `run_start`. It runs once per process, on the first combined quantize of the first
  `linear_proj`; no later layer or call is checked.
  - The "checked" flag is set first (L108), then the check runs (L109).
  - It makes two copies of the live quantizer, one row-only and one column-only, and quantizes the same input with each
    through `tex.quantize` (L43-48; `tex` is TE's C++ extension module).
  - It compares the combined call's row-wise data, scales and amax with the row-only result, and its column-wise data,
    scales and amax with the column-only result: shape, dtype and every byte (L32-37, L50-52). A buffer missing from the
    combined result fails (L52). It also requires the same GEMM-swizzle flag on all three (L53-55).
  - Every rank runs the check; the count of failing ranks is all-reduced (L57-59). Rank 0 prints the check line, and
    every rank raises `RuntimeError` if any rank failed (L60-69).
- **What the references are in the submitted configuration.** N6 replaces `tex.quantize` itself
  (`ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L1543), and TE's `quantize_impl` is `tex.quantize(tensor, self)` (TE
  `tensor/nvfp4_tensor.py` L253-255, read on `131157b5`).
  - The combined call and the column-only reference take N6's RHT-amax route, armed by
    `AK_NVFP4P_RHTAMAX=1` (config L24): K13's amax kernel,
    then the patch's cast (`ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L1354-1389, L1472-1476). The row-only reference takes TE's own
    quantize, because that route needs the column-wise usage (L1472-1473).
  - These are the calls the bundle makes with N8 off: a row-only quantize in the forward, a column-only one in the
    backward. So the check compares the bundle with N8 on against the bundle with N8 off, for the first input.
  - K13's own first-call checks compare that route with TE's unwrapped quantize: the combined call at `result_1.txt`
    L873 and the column-only reference at L874, both True, just before N8's line ([K13](K13_nvfp4bx_norm_bwd.md)).
    A column-only quantize of this input in the forward (L874) is N8's reference: the stock flow makes one only in the
    backward.
- **Run-start gate:** its `projcol` row passes when the check has run and at least one module was cleared
  (`firmus_ak/run_start_gate.py` L43-46), so an armed N8 whose hook never fired (Megatron no longer setting the flag, or
  no NVFP4 quantize reaching the check) stops the run before `run_start`. As the "checked" flag is set before the
  comparison, the row would also pass if a caller had caught the check's exception; nothing in the recipe catches it.
  The gate's verdict is per rank ([Enablement and fail-loud behaviour](../KERNELS.md#enablement-and-fail-loud-behaviour));
  N8's check all-reduces its failing-rank count, so every rank reaches the same verdict and raises together.
- **The check line** is one of the 56 proof lines that Firmus's post-run check requires in every scored log (R12). It
  carries a verdict but no file path or sha (R13); the module is pinned by the image's sha256 and its source
  record (Source).

## Approval (Approval)

None needed: E0. Graph Execution (TR-8.3) allows mathematically equivalent changes to the non-weight parts of the
computation. Here N8 selects TE's own default mode for one module; the quantizer, the kernels and the arithmetic are
TE's, and the bytes are equal. The cost is memory: about 34 MB of NVFP4 data per layer, held from the forward to the
backward (State).

## Evidence (Evidence)

**Result on the submitted image:** PASS: the kit found TE's two modes byte-identical in both forms, and the first-call
check was True in the smoke run and all ten scored runs; on L4 v2's image (same module) the unit test of the module's
own action found every output byte equal to stock, and the training loop with N8 off was identical over 200 steps.

### Tests on the submitted image

- **Image checks** (R15): importing `firmus_ak` in the clean image prints the banner `MATCH` and imports all eight patch
  modules; the kit runner's image check found `ak_l8b_projcol` equal to the package's copy (`17f0403a71ad567a`), build
  and source records verified. The kit below is one of the 24 re-targeted kits run on this image, 48 / 48 PASS (R14).
- **The kit for N8, PASS in both forms** (R14): a frozen development test suite, re-targeted at the image's installed files, run
  as written and with the allocator cache first filled with 148.1 GB of random bytes, one GPU each. It checks that the
  installed module and its copy in the recipe tree carry the source record's sha (`17f0403a…`, OK), locating the module
  without importing it.
  - **It does not run the shipped module: its test applies the module's change to TE itself** and compares TE's two
    modes, the core of the argument: two TE `Linear(4096, 4096, bias=False)` modules with one weight,
    `save_original_input` True (stock) and False (N8's state), TE's NVFP4 recipe, the gradients' stochastic rounding
    started from the same CUDA seed on both sides.
  - Inputs `[s, 2, 4096]` with s 8,192 (the recipe) and 1,024, Gaussian and an edge pattern (all-zero and −0.0 feature
    columns, a 1e4 outlier, bf16 subnormals): output, input gradient and weight gradient equal as bytes in all four
    cases, in both forms.
  - Its quantize-call count at s 8,192 shows the change: stock makes a row-only and a column-only quantize of the
    `[8192, 2, 4096]` input, N8's state one row-and-column quantize; the 2D weight's and the gradient's are the same.
- **The 2 × 4 smoke run** (R16): 800 steps of the submitted configuration on this image. The check line (smoke log
  L875) is the same, True; all 56 proof lines are present; the run-start gate line (L946) names `projcol` among its 19
  armed parts and ends `True`.

### Checks in every scored run

- The check line, once in each of the ten logs (`results/firmus_gb300_ngpu8_llama8b_l4_nvfp4_v3/llama31_8b/result_0.txt` … `result_9.txt`), at L875 in all ten, with
  identical text, ending `ranks failing 0: True`; no log contains `E0 self-check FAILED`. `result_1.txt` L875:

  ```text
  0: [auto_kernel projcol] linear_proj keeps its NVFP4 column-wise input from the forward ARMED: save_original_input cleared on 32 module(s); first forward quantize [8192, 2, 4096] torch.bfloat16 (row True col True, RHT True, SR False) v the row-only (stock forward) and column-only (stock backward) quantizes of the same input: {'rowwise_data': True, 'rowwise_scale_inv': True, 'amax_rowwise': True, 'columnwise_data': True, 'columnwise_scale_inv': True, 'amax_columnwise': True, 'swizzled_flag': True}; ranks failing 0: True
  ```

- In `result_1.txt`, L875 is in the forward of warm-up iteration 0 (L860-919), before the training graph capture
  (L921); K13's checks of the references' route are True just before it (L873, L874). The banner reports MATCH at L70;
  the gate line at L946 names `projcol` among its 19 armed parts and ends `True`; `run_start` follows at L950.

### Tests on L4 v2's image

L4 v2's submitted image; its files differ from L4 v3's only in N11's module, the run-start gate, the leaf's one added
switch, four comments or docstrings, and the three rebuilt extensions (K10, K11, K12). N8's module (`17f0403a`) and
the gate's `projcol` row (L43-46) are the same in both.

- **Unit test of the module's own action, PASS** (R3): the image's installed module (`17f0403a71ad567a`, MATCH with
  the package: R1), armed with L4 v2's leaf's switches, on the recipe's `linear_proj` (TE `Linear(4096, 4096,
  bias=False)`, bf16 parameters, the recipe's NVFP4 autocast, forward and backward on `[s, b, 4096]`).
  - *Reference:* the module as Megatron leaves it (`save_original_input=True`). *N8's side:* the same weight bytes with
    the module's own action applied as its `Attention.__init__` wrapper applies it (the flag cleared, the module
    counted, its forward wrapped by the module's `_wrap_proj_forward`). Both start the gradients' stochastic rounding
    from the same generator state. *Graded:* output, input gradient and weight gradient as bytes: equal in every case.
  - *Cases* (visible, reseeded, hidden, shape-variant and edge): 8,192 × 2 (training); 1,024 × 2; 1,024 × 2 with values
    scaled by powers of two from 2^-20 to 2^20; 2,048 × 1; hidden sequence lengths in steps of 64 (TE's stock NVFP4
    weight-gradient GEMM has no cuBLASLt algorithm for some other token counts, where the reference raised; the recipe
    sends 16,384 tokens); shape variants; the test plan's edge patterns on the input and the incoming gradient, and an
    all-zero input. It counts the row-and-column quantizes on N8's side, so a run in which the combined path never ran
    fails.
  - *Address and sequence forms, PASS* (R3, R2): the same cases with the inputs at other addresses, and in an eager,
    capture and replay sequence whose capture and replay step this site skips (the spec grades `linear_proj` eagerly;
    the training graph's capture of `linear_proj` runs in the model-level comparison).
- **Model-level comparison, PASS** (R4): the recipe's own training, with its full-iteration CUDA graph, in the image
  without an overlay; L4 v2's leaf sourced, then `AK_PROJCOL` unset. DP 4, mock data, one test seed; the loss of every
  logged step and the evaluation compared, with N8's line absent and every other check line present. At 200 steps, with
  an evaluation at step 200, the arm with N8 off was identical in full to both loops of the whole bundle. At 50 steps the
  two loops of the whole bundle departed from each other at step 45
  ([run-to-run reproducibility](../KERNELS.md#run-to-run-reproducibility)), and the arm with N8 off matched the first in
  full. So on that trajectory N8 changes nothing the loop logs, including in the captured training step and through
  the module's own `Attention.__init__` hook.
- **Coverage check** (R5): N8's one path, the combined quantize, is graded by the unit test, its address and sequence
  forms, and the model-level comparison. The kit, re-run with the leaf's switches unset as the kits' own runner runs
  them, also passed (R1).

### Training

N8 was on in all ten submitted runs, and its first-call line is True in each. Convergence is in the index.
